Declaring: a mcp.yaml resource with an entrypoint (an existing .tsx/.ts/.jsx/.js file under static/), tools (declared tool names it permits), data_schema, schema_version (1 or more) and an optional token-free deep_link is a reviewed component. deep_link is a path relative to the app host whose placeholders are declared scalar data_schema fields; a scheme, host, percent-encoding, dot segment, or token/code/secret anywhere refuses. Each of these fields is in the contract digest, so changing one invalidates pending intents; a manifest that does not use them keeps its digest. HTML entrypoints are declared but not published.

Binding a tool: a tool binds a component by setting its own `component:` to that resource's `uri` (for example `component: ui://notes/card`). The resource's `name` or its `component:` label is refused with `tool "<name>" has unresolved component resource`; `component: none` binds nothing.

Serving: the server advertises the resources capability only when the manifest declares one, and serves resources/list and resources/read for each as ui://<declared uri>@<closure hash> with MIME text/html;profile=mcp-app. Content is byte-identical for every caller (no tenant data, token, receipt, signed URL or identity is baked in), but listing and reading follow the tool grants: a caller sees a component only when allowed at least one tool bound to it, discovery and reads are private and re-authorized on every request.

Build: the page is built from the reviewed, digest-bound source only (no model-written code): the entrypoint and the vendored MCP Apps bundle are bundled into one self-contained inline module, with no source map, refusing any import outside static/ and any build error, and a CSP that allows no network, frame, object or base access and runs only that module by hash. The hash covers the entrypoint's whole import closure, the vendored bundle, the bridge, the data schema and the policy, so any change gives a new URI and a read of an old URI is not found. A build failure leaves the component unpublished (logged once per generation) while its tools keep working with the text envelope.

Tool metadata: a tool with component: carries _meta.ui.resourceUri (and the deprecated ui/resourceUri) only for a published component; when components are declared, every listed tool (built-in _commit, _status, artifact.export, command, file and external tools included) carries _meta.ui.visibility, which lists app only for tools some component permits or binds. A tool result still carries the text envelope, and _meta.deep_link when the component declares one: an absolute URL built from declared scalar data fields only, escaped, or omitted if a field is missing or mistyped.

Inside the widget: importing @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps gives the vendored App wrapped by a bridge that refuses tools outside the component's permitted set, caps calls (30 a minute) and argument size, and re-reads the linked tool on focus, visibility, reconnect, app.refresh(true) and a succeeded committed _status result; it never touches localStorage. The bridge limits are a guard for honest components; the server still authorizes every call per caller. Calls from a widget are ordinary tool calls.
